signals.title: USD — Geopolitical Headline + Macro Surprise
signals.text: The USD faces acute pressure as Trump headlines regarding the declaration of the Strait of Hormuz as US territory introduce significant geopolitical volatility while VIX remains at 14.2 (low volatility). This tension coincides with weak US retail sales and consumer sentiment reports which have actively curbed Fed rate-hike expectations, driving the DXY below its SMA20/50 cluster at 100.46/100.61. Despite a restrictive real rate of +1.52%, the USD is failing to attract safe-haven flows as the bear steepener yield curve regime (2s10s +49.6bp) suggests a focus on growth deceleration rather than funding stress. The market is now discounting higher-for-longer bets, leaving the Greenback vulnerable to further downside if FOMC minutes confirm a dovish tilt. Trade bias: Bearish USD; geopolitical headlines and weak data override the carry advantage. Catalyst: FOMC Minutes on 19 Aug. Risk: Escalation in the Strait of Hormuz triggers broad risk-off flows that revive the USD safe-haven bid.

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY displays a dominant G10 bilateral theme as the CAD outperforms with a 1W average of +1.062% while JPY remains the laggard at -1.002%, creating a 2.064% leader-to-laggard gap. The move is supported by a +125bp OIS carry advantage (CORRA 2.27% vs TONA 0.98%) and a constructive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) for CAD at +11.6 compared to USD weakness. JPY remains under pressure despite a strong positive ESI of +16.3 as the USD/JPY vs VIX correlation (z=+1.59σ) signals the JPY's safe-haven function is currently broken. Institutional research from Saxo Bank notes that long US yields have kept carry trades alive, supporting CAD/JPY longs in a low-volatility environment. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; carry and G10 momentum favor trend continuation. Catalyst: BoC meeting on 9 Sep — hold priced. Risk: VIX spikes above 20, forcing an unwind of the carry trade and narrowing the CAD/JPY spread.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Volatility + Retail
signals.text: GBP/USD has hit a three-month high at 1.3537, trading firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3370–1.3424). COT LF positioning is net long +39,039 (70.1% long), and retail sentiment is at a 75% short extreme, creating a classic institutional-vs-retail divergence that supports the current trend. Volatility pricing shows an elevated premium with GBP/USD IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 6.0%, suggesting the market is paying 5.0pts of VRP for upside protection as the USD slide deepens. Although the Fed-BoE OIS carry is neutral at 0bp, the GBP's restrictive real rate of +0.93% outpaces the ECB's +0.09%, making Sterling the preferred European yield play. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; contrarian retail shorting provides fuel for further extensions. Catalyst: UK Inflation data on 19 Aug. Risk: A sharp reversal in US retail sentiment or a hawkish FOMC surprise that forces a liquidation of the crowded spec long.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Positioning
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.32, holding below its SMA20/50 cluster at 160.65/161.12, reflecting growing caution near the 160.00 psychological level. The options market shows a strong downside bias with 1M 25d Risk Reversals at -2.08, even as the +264bp OIS carry differential favors the USD. COT data reveals a crowded JPY spec short of -63,633, which remains vulnerable to a squeeze if US data continues to disappoint or if BoJ hike pricing (currently bias: Hike) intensifies. The unusual complacency in options supply (VRP -1.3%) suggests that while the skew is bearish, the cost of protection has not yet spiked to reflect intervention risk. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; downside options skew and crowded shorts favor a technical retracement. Catalyst: BoJ meeting on 18 Sep. Risk: Fed-BoJ yield spread widens further, invalidating the bearish options skew and resuming the carry grind higher.
